title: One-Arm Standing Arnold Press
overview: The one-arm standing Arnold press is a variation of thestanding Arnold pressand an exercise utilized to build shoulder muscle size and strength.The Arnold press, named afterArnold Schwarzeneggerhimself, is an exercise used to target every single head of the deltoid.The exercise is best used by those seeking aesthetic benefits due to its long time under tension, but can also be used as an accessory movement by those attempting to build strength.Performing unilateral movements can help improve weaknesses, balance your strength and aesthetic physique, and work towards reducing injuries by addressing imbalances in the body.
instructions: Grab a dumbbell and assume a shoulder-width stance.
Raise the dumbbell to around shoulder height, and rotate your wrist so that your palm is facing your body. You can place your other hand on your waist for support. This is the starting position.
Slowly press the dumbbell overhead by extending the elbows and contracting the deltoids. As you press, rotate the dumbbell until your palm is facing forward.
Once your arm is almost fully extended, begin lowering the dumbbell back down to the starting position - rotating your wrist until your palm is facing your body once again.
Repeat this movement for the desired amount of reps, and then repeat with your other arm.
tips: Always use a full range of motion and control the dumbbell throughout the set.
As you press the dumbbell overhead, exhale and drive the bicep to the ear.
If you sense any pressure in your neck or traps during the movement, look to address a lack ofthoracic spine extensionorshoulder flexion.
If you have lower back problems, theseated Arnold pressmay be a better version to try.
